core_obligations: Reduction to the plus construction (proof lines 10207-10212): it suffices to compare the plus constructions, because the plus construction of the given presheaf again satisfies the hypothesis of the lemma.

The two colimits (proof lines 10213-10226): the author writes both sides as colimits over coverings, one over coverings of the image in the target site and one over images of coverings of the object in the source site, noting that images of coverings are coverings by continuity.

The comparison (proof lines 10227-10243): the author compares the two colimit expressions, using the behaviour of compatible families over coverings with sheaf theoretically empty members, and concludes using almost cocontinuity, which allows any covering of the image to be refined by the image of a covering of the object.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to comparing the plus constructions.
Write both sides as colimits over coverings.
Compare using the hypothesis on values at sheaf theoretically empty objects and almost cocontinuity.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a continuous and almost cocontinuous functor and a presheaf whose values at sheaf theoretically empty objects are singletons, sheafifying the inverse image gives the same result as applying the inverse image to the sheafification (statement lines 10196-10204). The proof is a complete computation: the assertion is reduced to comparing the plus constructions, since the plus construction preserves the hypothesis (proof lines 10207-10212); both sides are written as colimits over coverings of the image and of the object (proof lines 10213-10226); and the comparison of the two colimits uses the hypothesis on values at sheaf theoretically empty objects together with almost cocontinuity, which lets any covering of the image be refined by the image of a covering of the object (proof lines 10227-10243). The non-formal content is the comparison of the two colimits. The claim is H2: a structured computation with each input named.
